questions.stem: A company wants to stop buying servers based on forecasts of next year's demand. Which advantage of cloud computing addresses this?

options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale
options.rationale: Economies of scale lower prices; they do not remove the need to forecast capacity.

options.text: Go global in minutes
options.rationale: Global deployment is about reaching users in more Regions, not about capacity planning.

options.text: Stop spending money running data centers
options.rationale: This is about operating facilities, not about sizing capacity.

options.text: Stop guessing capacity
options.rationale: You use the capacity you need now and scale up or down in minutes, instead of buying hardware for a forecast.

questions.explanation: Stop guessing capacity is one of the six advantages of cloud computing: access as much or as little capacity as you need and scale in minutes.

questions.stem: A company wants to deploy its application in several geographic Regions with a few clicks so users worldwide get lower latency. Which advantage of cloud computing is this?

options.text: Go global in minutes
options.rationale: AWS lets you deploy in multiple Regions around the world quickly, giving users lower latency at low cost.

options.text: Stop guessing capacity
options.rationale: Capacity planning is a different advantage.

options.text: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
options.rationale: This advantage is about how you pay, not where you deploy.

options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale
options.rationale: This advantage explains lower prices, not global reach.

questions.explanation: Go global in minutes: deploy in multiple Regions with a few clicks to provide lower latency and a better experience for customers.

questions.stem: Why can AWS offer lower pay-as-you-go prices than most companies could achieve running their own data centers?

options.text: AWS requires each customer to sign a multi-year contract before using it
options.rationale: Most AWS services are pay-as-you-go with no long-term contract required.

options.text: Usage from many customers is aggregated, creating economies of scale
options.rationale: Aggregated usage across a very large customer base lets AWS achieve higher economies of scale and pass savings on.

options.text: Customers share physical servers without any isolation
options.rationale: AWS isolates customers; low prices do not come from removing isolation.

options.text: AWS bills for stored data but does not bill for compute
options.rationale: Compute is billed; pricing is not limited to storage.

questions.explanation: Because usage from hundreds of thousands of customers is aggregated in the cloud, AWS achieves higher economies of scale, which translates into lower pay-as-you-go prices.

questions.stem: Which term describes acquiring resources when demand rises and releasing them when demand falls, so capacity follows the workload?

options.text: Durability
options.rationale: Durability is about not losing stored data.

options.text: High availability
options.rationale: High availability is about staying up when components fail.

options.text: Elasticity
options.rationale: Elasticity is the ability to scale resources up and down automatically with demand.

options.text: Data sovereignty
options.rationale: Data sovereignty is about where data is stored and which laws apply.

questions.explanation: Elasticity lets a workload use only the capacity it needs at any moment, which avoids paying for idle resources.

questions.stem: A company runs its application in multiple Availability Zones so the application keeps working if one data center has a problem. Which benefit does this provide?

options.text: Elasticity
options.rationale: Elasticity is about scaling with demand, not about surviving failures.

options.text: Economies of scale
options.rationale: Economies of scale are about lower costs.

options.text: Agility
options.rationale: Agility is about how quickly you can experiment and deliver.

options.text: High availability
options.rationale: Spreading the workload across Availability Zones removes single points of failure.

questions.explanation: Availability Zones are isolated from each other, so running in more than one keeps the application available when a single location fails.

questions.stem: Developers can now launch a new test environment in minutes instead of waiting weeks for hardware. Which cloud benefit does this describe?

options.text: Increased speed and agility
options.rationale: Resources are a click away, so the time to make them available drops from weeks to minutes.

options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale
options.rationale: Economies of scale are about price, not delivery speed.

options.text: High availability
options.rationale: High availability is about resilience to failure.

options.text: Stop guessing capacity
options.rationale: This advantage is about capacity planning rather than how fast teams can experiment.

questions.explanation: Increased speed and agility: new IT resources are only a click away, which lowers the cost and time of experimentation.

questions.stem: A startup wants to pay only for the computing it consumes rather than investing heavily in servers before it knows how it will use them. Which advantage applies?

options.text: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
options.rationale: This advantage is about who operates the facilities, not how you pay.

options.text: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
options.rationale: Instead of up-front data center investment, you pay only when you consume resources, and only for how much.

options.text: Increase speed and agility
options.rationale: Agility is about how fast resources are available, not how they are paid for.

options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale
options.rationale: Economies of scale explain lower prices, not the shift from up-front to usage-based spending.

questions.explanation: Trading fixed (capital) expense for variable expense means paying only for the resources you consume instead of investing in data centers and servers up front.

questions.stem: Which advantage of cloud computing lets a company focus on its customers instead of racking, stacking and powering servers?

options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale
options.rationale: Economies of scale lower prices; this question is about where staff spend their effort.

options.text: Increase speed and agility so teams can deliver features faster
options.rationale: Agility is about how quickly teams deliver, not about who runs the infrastructure.

options.text: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
options.rationale: AWS handles the heavy lifting of facilities and hardware, so the company can focus on its own projects.

options.text: Stop guessing capacity
options.rationale: This advantage is about capacity planning.

questions.explanation: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers: focus on projects that differentiate the business, not on infrastructure.

questions.stem: How does the AWS global infrastructure help a company serve users on several continents with low latency?

options.text: All AWS traffic is routed through one central Region
options.rationale: AWS Regions operate independently; traffic is not funneled through a single Region.

options.text: AWS upgrades the home internet connection of every user
options.rationale: AWS does not control end users' internet connections.

options.text: Edge locations run the company's databases by default
options.rationale: Edge locations cache content; they do not host your databases by default.

options.text: It can deploy resources in Regions located close to those users
options.rationale: Regions around the world let you place workloads near your users.

questions.explanation: Choosing Regions close to users reduces network distance, and therefore latency, for those users.

questions.stem: Which TWO are benefits of moving workloads to the AWS Cloud? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Physical access to AWS data centers for customer audits
options.rationale: Customers do not get physical access; AWS provides audit reports through AWS Artifact instead.

options.text: The ability to scale resources up or down quickly
options.rationale: Capacity can follow demand in minutes.

options.text: Unlimited free compute for the first year
options.rationale: The AWS Free Tier is limited; compute is not unlimited or free.

options.text: Pay-as-you-go pricing for the resources used
options.rationale: You pay for what you use, with no large up-front investment.

options.text: No security responsibilities for the customer
options.rationale: Customers keep security responsibilities under the shared responsibility model.

questions.explanation: Variable, usage-based pricing and elastic capacity are core cloud benefits. Security remains shared between AWS and the customer.

questions.stem: A startup based in the United States wants to serve customers in Europe. How does the AWS global infrastructure help?

options.text: Data transfer between continents becomes free
options.rationale: Inter-Region data transfer is still charged.

options.text: AWS translates the application for European users
options.rationale: Infrastructure does not translate applications.

options.text: The company is exempt from European data laws
options.rationale: Using AWS does not remove legal obligations.

options.text: It can launch resources in a European Region without building a data center
options.rationale: Regions around the world let you deploy close to new markets in minutes.

questions.explanation: Global reach without building facilities is one of the main benefits of the AWS Cloud.

questions.stem: How does the AWS Cloud lower the cost of trying out a new idea?

options.text: Resources can be started for a test and shut down, paying for the time used
options.rationale: Experiments cost little because you stop paying when you turn resources off.

options.text: AWS refunds the cost of experiments that fail
options.rationale: AWS does not refund usage based on outcomes.

options.text: Experiments in the cloud have no usage charges
options.rationale: Usage is billed, apart from limited free offers.

options.text: Hardware for experiments ships faster to the office
options.rationale: Cloud resources are virtual; nothing ships to you.

questions.explanation: Low-cost experimentation is part of the speed and agility advantage.

questions.stem: An online store gets ten times its normal traffic during a yearly sale. Which cloud characteristic lets it handle the peak without paying for idle capacity the rest of the year?

options.text: Durability
options.rationale: Durability is about not losing stored data.

options.text: Elasticity
options.rationale: Capacity grows for the peak and shrinks afterwards, so you pay only for what you use.

options.text: Data sovereignty
options.rationale: Data sovereignty is about where data is stored.

options.text: Fixed capacity planning
options.rationale: Fixed capacity is what the cloud lets you avoid.

questions.explanation: Elasticity matches resources to demand automatically.

questions.stem: What does fault tolerance mean for a workload?

options.text: It scales resources up and down with demand
options.rationale: That describes elasticity.

options.text: It keeps its data stored inside one country
options.rationale: That describes data residency.

options.text: It keeps operating without interruption when some components fail
options.rationale: A fault-tolerant design has redundancy so a component failure does not stop the system.

options.text: It runs at the lowest possible monthly cost
options.rationale: That describes cost optimization.

questions.explanation: Fault tolerance and high availability are both benefits of building across multiple Availability Zones.

questions.stem: AWS has reduced its prices many times as its customer base has grown. Which advantage of cloud computing explains this?

options.text: Go global in minutes
options.rationale: Global reach is about where you can deploy.

options.text: Stop guessing capacity
options.rationale: Capacity planning is about sizing, not price levels.

options.text: Increase speed and agility
options.rationale: Agility is about how quickly you can deliver.

options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale
options.rationale: Higher aggregate usage lets AWS lower its costs and pass the savings on to customers.

questions.explanation: Economies of scale translate into lower pay-as-you-go prices.

questions.stem: Which TWO are among the six advantages of cloud computing described by AWS? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
options.rationale: Pay for what you consume instead of investing up front.

options.text: Unlimited storage at no charge
options.rationale: Storage is billed.

options.text: Go global in minutes
options.rationale: Deploy in multiple Regions around the world with a few clicks.

options.text: Zero downtime for every application, by contract
options.rationale: AWS designs for high availability, but zero downtime is not guaranteed for your application.

options.text: Physical control of the servers you use
options.rationale: Customers do not get physical control of AWS hardware.

questions.explanation: The six advantages: trade fixed for variable expense, economies of scale, stop guessing capacity, speed and agility, stop running data centers, and go global in minutes.
